data.gender_notes: Bhuban is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhuban is a Sanskrit name derived from the root Bhuh, which means 'earth'. The name Bhuban signifies the lord or ruler of the earth. It is a name with deep spiritual roots and is commonly used in Hindu mythology. The name Bhuban carries the meaning “Lord of the earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhuban usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of earthly power and stability

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhuban total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bhuban is an integral part of Hindu culture, symbolizing the connection between humanity and the earth. In Hinduism, gods and goddesses are often depicted as ruling over different aspects of nature, and Bhuban as the lord of the earth reflects this belief. Furthermore, it is believed that performing certain rituals and ceremonies on the land named Bhuban can bring good fortune and blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bhuban holds significant spiritual meaning, representing the divine presence and relationship between humans and the earth. In Hinduism, the earth is considered the physical manifestation of the goddess Prithvi, and honoring and respecting the earth and its deities is an essential aspect of spiritual practice. The name embodies the idea that we are not separate from the earth but are an integral part of it. Moreover, it is a reminder of the need to live in harmony with nature and honor the natural world for its abundance and sustenance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhuban symbolizes the divine cosmic energy that sustains the universe. It represents the eternal presence of the divine in the material world, nurturing and protecting all creation.

historical_references.reference: Bhuban is an ancient name for the city of Bhubaneswar, which was the capital of the Kesari and Ganga dynasties in ancient India. The city was known as 'Tataka' during the Kesari kingdom (3rd to 6th century CE), but was later renamed 'Bhubaneswar' by King Anangabhima III of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty in the 13th century CE.
historical_references.context: Capital city of ancient Indian dynasties

historical_references.reference: Bhuban is also the name of a temple town in the present-day Indian state of West Bengal. The town was famously referred to as 'Bhuban-Mahasthana' in the 16th century CE text, 'The Ananda Vardhana', which describes it as a center of Shaiva worship. The temple town is believed to have been a significant religious center during the medieval period.
historical_references.context: Temple town and center of Shaiva worship

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Bhuban' is derived from the Sanskrit word meaning 'to build'. In the modern context, it is seen on three distinct platforms: Google Maps, where it refers to a place building functionality; the Smart Cities Initiative, where it represents the concept of building sustainable urban environments; and meditation apps, where it is used as a meditative mantra to help build inner peace and focus. The general trend is towards leveraging technology and spiritual practices to build more efficient, sustainable, and peaceful societies.
